+    ignore:
+      - '^unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section\.'

+# Issue 340 / PR 341 work plan
+
+Objective: address every requirement of issue 340 in PR 341, with evidence and
+verification, without merging the pull request.

+- [ ] Read the full issue, sub-issues, all three PR comment types and latest feedback.

+- [ ] Read the CI/CD best practices and compare the complete file trees and every
+      workflow/CI script in the JS, Rust and Python templates with this repository.
+- [ ] Record the event timeline, exhaustive requirement inventory, root causes,
+      online primary-source research, existing components and solution choices.
+- [ ] Reproduce each defect with focused tests; implement all applicable fixes
+      across workflows/scripts. Add opt-in diagnostics if evidence is insufficient.
+- [ ] Report reproduced template/upstream defects with examples, workarounds and
+      suggested code fixes, when applicable.
+- [ ] Add release triggers required by repository conventions, commit useful
+      atomic steps, and push only issue-340-8f7dd340a8ef.
+- [ ] Inspect the complete PR diff; merge latest main into this branch if needed;
+      run focused checks, then inspect all current-SHA CI runs and preserve logs.
+- [ ] Update PR title/body with reproduction, tests, findings and Fixes #340;
+      verify a clean worktree and mark PR 341 ready only after required checks pass.
+
+Local constraints: 2.92 GiB total container memory; prefer static checks and small
+script tests. Leave full builds/test matrices to CI. Keep experiments bounded and
+put reusable probes under experiments/issue-340/.

+# CI/CD Best Practices for AI-Driven Development (languages: en • [zh](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.zh.md) • [hi](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.hi.md) • [ru](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.ru.md))
+
+This document describes CI/CD best practices that significantly improve the quality and reliability of AI-driven development workflows. When properly configured, Hive Mind AI solvers are forced to iterate with CI/CD checks until all tests pass, ensuring code quality meets the highest standards.
+
+## Why CI/CD Matters for AI Development
+
+Hive Mind's AI issue solver is instructed to pay attention to CI/CD checks in each pull request. This creates a powerful feedback loop:
+
+1. **AI creates a solution** - The solver generates code based on issue requirements
+2. **CI/CD validates the solution** - Automated checks verify code quality
+3. **AI iterates until passing** - The solver fixes issues until all checks pass
+4. **Quality is guaranteed** - No code merges without passing all gates
+
+This approach ensures consistent quality regardless of whether the team consists of humans, AIs, or both.
+
+## Recommended CI/CD Templates
+
+We provide ready-to-use templates for multiple languages with all best practices pre-configured:
+
+| Language              | Template Repository                                                                                                                 |
+| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | [js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)         |
+| Rust                  | [rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)     |
+| Python                | [python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) |
+| Go                    | [go-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/go-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)         |
+| C#                    | [csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) |
+| Java                  | [java-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/java-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)     |
+| C/C++                 | [cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)       |
+| PHP                   | [php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template](https://github.com/link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template)       |
+
+> **Tip:** You don't have to pick a template by hand. Run `fix <repository-url> --ci-cd` (see [Automatic CI/CD Remediation](#automatic-cicd-remediation)) and Hive Mind detects the repository's languages and selects the matching templates for you.
+
+## Key CI/CD Principles
+
+> **Pin hosted runner operating systems.** Mutable aliases such as
+> `ubuntu-latest` can switch major OS versions without a repository diff and
+> emit migration notices. Use an explicit supported label such as
+> `ubuntu-24.04`, then upgrade in a dedicated compatibility PR.
+
+### 1. Run Checks Only on Relevant File Changes
+
+**Only trigger checks when relevant files change.** This dramatically reduces CI costs and run times.
+
+Use a `detect-changes` job at the start of your workflow to determine which file categories changed:
+
+```yaml
+jobs:
+  detect-changes:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    outputs:
+      code-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.code }}
+      docs-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docs }}
+      docker-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.docker }}
+      workflow-changed: ${{ steps.changes.outputs.workflow }}
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 2
+      - name: Detect changes
+        id: changes
+        run: node scripts/detect-code-changes.mjs
+```
+
+Then gate each job on the relevant output:
+
+```yaml
+test-suites:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.code-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
+  # ...
+
+validate-docs:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'
+  # ...
+
+docker-pr-check:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docker-changed == 'true' || needs.detect-changes.outputs.workflow-changed == 'true'
+  # ...
+```
+
+**What to exclude from "code changes" detection:**
+
+- Markdown files (`*.md`) — documentation-only changes don't need changeset files
+- `.changeset/` folder — changeset metadata isn't code
+- `data/` and `experiments/` folders — non-production content
+- `.gitkeep` files — placeholder files with no functional impact
+
+**What always triggers checks when changed:**
+
+- Source code files (`.mjs`, `.ts`, `.py`, `.rs`, `.go`, etc.)
+- `package.json` / dependency manifests
+- CI/CD workflow files (`.github/workflows/*.yml`)
+- `Dockerfile` and related infrastructure files
+
+### 2. File Size Limits
+
+**Enforce a maximum of 1000-1500 lines per code file.**
+
+This constraint benefits both AI and human developers:
+
+- AI models can read and understand entire files within context windows
+- Humans can navigate and comprehend files without cognitive overload
+- Forces modular, well-organized code architecture
+
+Example enforcement in CI (bash):
+
+```bash
+find src/ -name "*.mjs" -type f | while read -r file; do
+  line_count=$(wc -l < "$file")
+  if [ "$line_count" -gt 1500 ]; then
+    echo "ERROR: $file has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)"
+    echo "::error file=$file::File has $line_count lines (limit: 1500)"
+    exit 1
+  fi
+done
+```
+
+**Synchronize the file-size ESLint rule with the CI check** to catch violations locally before CI:
+
+```js
+// eslint.config.mjs
+{
+  rules: {
+    'max-lines': ['error', { max: 1500 }]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+### 3. Automated Code Formatting
+
+Consistent formatting eliminates style debates and reduces diff noise:
+
+| Language              | Tool                          |
+| --------------------- | ----------------------------- |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | ESLint + Prettier             |
+| Rust                  | rustfmt                       |
+| Python                | Ruff                          |
+| Go                    | gofmt                         |
+| C#                    | dotnet format                 |
+| Java                  | Spotless (Google Java Format) |
+| C/C++                 | clang-format                  |
+| PHP                   | PHP CS Fixer                  |
+
+All templates include pre-commit hooks that run formatters automatically before each commit.
+
+### 4. Static Analysis & Linting
+
+Catch bugs and enforce patterns before code reaches review:
+
+| Language              | Tools                                      |
+| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | ESLint with strict rules                   |
+| Rust                  | Clippy (pedantic + nursery)                |
+| Python                | Ruff + mypy                                |
+| Go                    | go vet + staticcheck                       |
+| C#                    | .NET analyzers (warnings as errors)        |
+| Java                  | SpotBugs (maximum effort)                  |
+| C/C++                 | clang-tidy + cppcheck (warnings as errors) |
+| PHP                   | PHPStan (max level)                        |
+
+### 5. Fast-Fail Job Ordering
+
+**Run fast checks before slow checks** to give the fastest possible feedback:
+
+```
+Fast checks (~7-30s each):     Slow checks (~1-10 min each):
+├── test-compilation            ├── test-suites (unit tests)
+├── lint (format + ESLint)      ├── test-execution (integration)
+└── check-file-line-limits      ├── docker-pr-check
+                                └── helm-pr-check
+```
+
+Gate slow checks on fast checks:
+
+```yaml
+test-suites:
+  needs: [test-compilation, lint, check-file-line-limits]
+  if: |
+    always() &&
+    !cancelled() &&
+    !contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') &&
+    needs.test-compilation.result == 'success' &&
+    needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
+    needs.check-file-line-limits.result == 'success'
+```
+
+### 6. Changeset-Based Versioning
+
+All templates use a changeset system that:
+
+- **Eliminates merge conflicts** - Each PR creates an independent changeset file
+- **Automates version bumps** - Highest bump type wins when merging
+- **Generates changelogs** - Release notes are compiled automatically
+- **Supports semantic versioning** - patch/minor/major bumps are explicit
+
+| Language              | Tool                         |
+| --------------------- | ---------------------------- |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | @changesets/cli              |
+| Rust                  | changelog.d + custom scripts |
+| Python                | Scriv                        |
+| PHP                   | changelog.d + custom scripts |
+| C/C++                 | changelog.d + custom scripts |
+| Go, C#, Java          | Custom changeset workflows   |
+
+**Exempt docs-only PRs from changeset requirements:**
+
+```yaml
+changeset-check:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'
+```
+
+Documentation-only changes (updating `.md` files) should not require a version bump.
+
+### 7. Validate the Actual Merge Result
+
+**CI must test what will actually be merged, not a stale PR snapshot.**
+
+When a PR is opened against a base branch that later receives new commits, the GitHub merge preview can become stale. Simulate a fresh merge before running checks:
+
+```yaml
+- name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)
+  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+  env:
+    BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}
+  run: |
+    git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
+    git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
+    git fetch origin "$BASE_REF"
+    BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)
+    if [ "$BEHIND_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
+      git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit || \
+        (echo "::error::Merge conflict! PR must be rebased before merging." && exit 1)
+    fi
+```
+
+This ensures lint, file-size, and other checks validate the final merged state.
+
+### 8. Pre-commit Hooks
+
+Local quality gates prevent broken commits from reaching CI:
+
+1. Format check and auto-fix
+2. Lint and static analysis
+3. Type checking (where applicable)
+4. File size validation
+5. Secrets detection
+
+This "shift left" approach catches issues immediately rather than waiting for CI.
+
+### 9. Release Automation
+
+Automated release workflows ensure:
+
+- **No manual version management** - Versions update automatically
+- **OIDC trusted publishing** - No API tokens needed in CI (npm, PyPI, crates.io)
+- **Validated releases only** - All checks must pass before publishing
+- **Dual trigger modes** - Both automatic (on merge) and manual (workflow dispatch)
+- **Commit the version bump directly to the default branch** - The release job pushes its generated version commit (package metadata, lockfile, changelog, consumed changesets) straight to `main` as `github-actions[bot]`, and fails closed if that commit changes anything other than release metadata. Do not route it through an auto-merged release pull request: every release then adds one more pull request and one more branch (a no-deletion ruleset keeps it forever), and a failed run leaves an open release pull request behind for someone to close
+- **A rule-blocked push is fixed in the rule, not in the workflow** - When a repository rule rejects the version push, fail the release with the rule's output and fix the rule (remove it, or add `github-actions` as a bypass actor). The rebase-and-retry path for a lost race is a different recovery for a rejection that prints the same word (see principle 10)
+- **Wait for the registry as long as it really takes, and never republish to find out** - `npm publish` can succeed minutes before `npm view` sees the version. Hive Mind's lag went from 2–9 s to 99–377 s in September 2026, and 2.35.1 took 874 s (issue #2923). A 330 s window turned a good release into a red run with no GitHub release, Docker image or Helm chart. Size the window from measured data with a wide margin (`experiments/npm-publish-lag-2923.mjs` measures it from the Sigstore attestations), log how long each wait took, and treat `E409 Cannot publish over previously staged version` as "already landed", not as a failure
+- **Decide "is there anything to release?" from every artifact, not just the registry** - If the job dies after the publish, the next push sees the version on npm and skips the release for good. Check the GitHub release too and re-run the release without a bump when it is missing; a lookup that fails is "unknown", which never releases
+
+**Prohibit manual version changes** in PRs — all version bumps should be managed by the CI release workflow:
+
+```yaml
+version-check:
+  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
+  steps:
+    - name: Check for version changes in package.json
+      run: node scripts/check-version.mjs
+```
+
+### 10. Concurrency Control
+
+**Separate cancellable read-only checks from non-cancellable write jobs.** Configure concurrency at the job level when a workflow contains both kinds of work:
+
+```yaml
+jobs:
+  lint:
+    # Include the job identity (and matrix values, when present) so unrelated
+    # checks remain parallel while a newer run replaces only the stale check.
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-lint
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    # ...
+
+  deploy:
+    needs: [lint]
+    if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.lint.result == 'success' }}
+    # Every job that writes to main or an external deployment target uses this
+    # repository-wide group, even when the jobs live in different workflows.
+    concurrency:
+      group: main-writer-${{ github.repository }}-main
+      cancel-in-progress: false
+    # ...
+```
+
+- **Read-only jobs:** Cancel superseded checks on both pull requests and `main` to reduce runner load. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.
+- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.
+- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.
+- **Workflow scope:** Do not put cancellable concurrency at workflow level when the workflow has write jobs. Cancelling the workflow would also interrupt a writer that has already started.
+
+By default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.
+
+Use `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.
+
+**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:
+
+```
+ ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)
+```
+
+The bullets above without this one convert "two writers collide" into "the second writer reliably fails" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.
+
+**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.
+
+**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — "Changes must be made through a pull request") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.
+
+```js
+for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {
+  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);
+  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };
+  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.
+  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });
+  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.
+  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);
+  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);
+}
+```
+
+- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.
+- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. Re-read the state instead of replaying the plan.
+- **Report success only after the push landed.** A step that sets `version_committed=true` before the push is confirmed leaves the downstream publish job working from a commit that exists only on that runner.
+- **Bound the retries and name the reason in the log.** A handful of attempts with a short delay covers a queue; an unbounded loop against a branch that is genuinely protected turns a fast failure into a long one.
+
+### 11. Secrets Detection
+
+Prevent accidental credential leaks in CI:
+
+- Include a secrets scan step using tools like `secretlint` or `truffleHog`
+- Fail CI immediately if secrets are detected
+- Never log environment variables or token values
+
+### 12. Documentation Validation
+
+**Validate documentation files in CI just like code:**
+
+- Check file size limits (e.g., max 2500 lines for docs)
+- Verify required sections exist in key documents
+- Check for broken links using tools like `lychee`
+
+```yaml
+validate-docs:
+  needs: [detect-changes]
+  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'
+  steps:
+    - run: node tests/docs-validation.mjs
+```
+
+### 13. Container Images: Native Runners per Architecture
+
+**Build each architecture on its own native runner.** GitHub provides free arm64 Linux runners for public repositories (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`). Emulating arm64 with QEMU on an x86 runner is much slower for compiled languages, and building two architectures inside one job makes them sequential instead of parallel.
+
+```yaml
+build-image:
+  strategy:
+    matrix:
+      include:
+        - platform: linux/amd64
+          runner: ubuntu-24.04
+        - platform: linux/arm64
+          runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
+  runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
+  steps:
+    - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
+      with:
+        platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}
+        cache-from: type=gha
+        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
+        outputs: type=image,push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true
+
+merge-manifest:
+  needs: [build-image]
+  steps:
+    - run: docker buildx imagetools create -t $IMAGE:$VERSION $DIGESTS
+```
+
+- **No `setup-qemu-action`.** Its presence means an architecture is being emulated; use a native runner instead.
+- **Publish images for every architecture your users run.** A single-architecture image silently excludes Apple Silicon, Graviton, and arm CI runners.
+- **Always cache.** Set `cache-from: type=gha` and `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max` on every build step; otherwise every architecture rebuilds the full dependency tree for every release.
+- **Never gate the release on the image push.** Publish the GitHub Release and language-registry package first, then attach images as they finish. Release notes contain no data derived from image bytes, so a slow or failed registry push must not hide an otherwise completed release.
+- **Assert what you shipped.** Verify that the published manifest lists every intended platform and that each default-branch tag has a corresponding GitHub Release; a missing release is otherwise easy to overlook.
+
+Reference implementations: [`link-foundation/box`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box) and [`link-assistant/hive-mind`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind).
+
+### 14. Lint the Workflows Themselves
+
+**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.
+
+Two complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:
+
+- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.
+- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.
+
+```yaml
+- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12
+  with:
+    args: -color
+```
+
+- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.
+- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.
+- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.
+- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.
+
+### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree
+
+**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.
+
+```yaml
+- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high
+```
+
+- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.
+- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.
+- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.
+
+### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build
+
+**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.
+
+Put a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.
+
+```yaml
+release-preflight:
+  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+  permissions:
+    contents: read
+    id-token: write # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it
+  steps:
+    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+    - env:
+        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}
+      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode "$PREFLIGHT_MODE"
+
+release:
+  needs: [release-preflight]
+  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}
+```
+
+- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.
+- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.
+- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.
+- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: write` + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:`) both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: write` is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.
+- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.
+- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: "0 verified, 3 unknown" is actionable, "no failures" is not.
+
+### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World
+
+**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.
+
+```yaml
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      bump_type:
+        required: true
+        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it
+```
+
+- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** "A newer version was published" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.
+- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.
+- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.
+- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.
+- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.
+- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as "tested". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).
+- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says "recovered and completed successfully" and then "❌ Agent reported error" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.
+
+## Quality Enforcement Strategy
+
+The templates implement a defense-in-depth approach:
+
+```
+Developer Machine    →    CI/CD Pipeline    →    Release
+├── Pre-commit hooks      ├── detect-changes      ├── All checks pass
+├── Local tests           ├── version-check       ├── Version bump
+└── IDE integration       ├── changeset-check     ├── Changelog update
+                          ├── test-compilation    └── Publish package
+                          ├── lint (format+ESLint)
+                          ├── check-file-line-limits
+                          ├── test-suites
+                          ├── test-execution
+                          ├── validate-docs
+                          └── docker-pr-check
+```
+
+Each layer catches different issues, ensuring no problematic code reaches production.
+
+## Getting Started
+
+1. **Choose a template** from the table above matching your language
+2. **Use it as a GitHub template** to create your new repository
+3. **Configure secrets** if needed for publishing (OIDC preferred)
+4. **Start developing** with all best practices pre-configured
+
+The AI solvers will automatically respect and iterate with all configured checks, producing higher quality output than repositories without CI/CD enforcement.
+
+## Automatic CI/CD Remediation
+
+For an existing repository, you don't need to apply these practices by hand. The `fix` command automates the whole flow:
+
+```bash
+fix https://github.com/owner/repo --ci-cd
+```
+
+This command:
+
+1. **Detects the repository's languages** using the GitHub Linguist API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages`), ordered by the number of bytes per language.
+2. **Selects the matching CI/CD templates** from the table above, sorted so the template for the most-used language comes first.
+3. **Inspects the latest default-branch run of every active workflow** by enumerating the workflow inventory, reading each workflow's time-ordered runs, and validating `head_branch` locally (GitHub's workflow-specific branch index can lag). This catches a failed required workflow on an earlier commit even when a busy workflow fills GitHub's 1,000-result combined-history window or the latest commit has unrelated passing runs, without permanently reporting a deleted workflow's last failure. If an inventory or per-workflow query fails, it falls back to paginated combined branch history; the exact latest-commit query is used only when branch history has no active runs.
+4. **Creates a remediation issue** that lists the failing runs, the detected languages, the recommended templates, and a link back to this document. The issue is created as a **Bug** (with a `bug` label) and its title and text are taken from the [standard remediation template](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139).
+5. **Hands the issue off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`**, which iterates until the fixes are merged. Every option `fix` does not consume itself (for example `--tool`, `--model`, `--think`) is forwarded to `/solve`.
+
+### Why the issue is a Bug, and what it leaves out
+
+`--development-log` replaces the template's retired case-study-folder instruction and collects artifacts under `./dev/log/issues/{issue-id}/pulls/{pull-id}`. `/fix` never emits the retired paragraph, including with `--no-solve` or partial option sets. `--deep-analysis` supplies the timeline, root-cause, debug-output, and upstream-reporting guidance, so `fix` conditionally omits the matching paragraphs instead of delivering them twice.
+
+That omission is only lossless because `/solve` emits the root-cause wording **only for bug-typed issues** — which is why `fix` creates the issue as a Bug. Issue types are configured per organization and labels per repository, so if the target repository accepts neither, the issue is still created without them.
+
+The retired paragraph cannot be restored by an option combination; `--development-log` is the only supported collection workflow. The remaining conditional omissions are controlled by `--deep-analysis`.
+
+### Language → Template Mapping
+
+The command maps detected languages to templates as follows (JavaScript and TypeScript share a single template, and so do C, C++ and CMake):
+
+| Detected Language(s)  | Template                                                         |
+| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| JavaScript/TypeScript | `link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |
+| Rust                  | `link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |
+| Python                | `link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |
+| Go                    | `link-foundation/go-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`     |
+| C#                    | `link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` |
+| Java                  | `link-foundation/java-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`   |
+| C/C++, CMake          | `link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |
+| PHP                   | `link-foundation/php-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`    |
+
+Languages without a dedicated template (for example Shell or Dockerfile) are listed in the issue for awareness, and the closest matching template is recommended.
+
+Use `--dry-run` to preview the issue without creating it, and `--no-solve` to create the issue without starting `/solve`:
+
+```bash
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --dry-run
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --no-solve
+```
+
+The issue is created as soon as the repository has been inspected, but `/solve` starts only after no GitHub Actions run is pending on the default branch, so the AI work never starts from a moving default branch or reasons about runs that are about to change. The wait polls every 30 seconds, gives up after `--ci-wait-timeout <minutes>` (default 60) and is skipped with `--no-wait-for-ci`. While it lasts, the Telegram reply shows a separate "⏳ Waiting for CI/CD" status with the runs still in progress, and when runs finished during the wait their latest results are commented on the issue ([issue #3326](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/3326)):
+
+```bash
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --ci-wait-timeout 30
+fix owner/repo --ci-cd --no-wait-for-ci
+```

+Real GitHub Hello World E2E runs create issues, pull requests and fixture branches. Keep `ENABLE_REAL_GITHUB_E2E` unset by default: schedule and `workflow_run` execution are opt-in through the optional repository variable `ENABLE_REAL_GITHUB_E2E=true`, while manual dispatch remains available. Default unit tests replay captured Agent, Claude and Codex output and verify run-bound evidence. Real runs still require physical fixture cleanup; protected branches keep the run red. Captured regression passes do not establish full #1483 or cross-client delivery acceptance.
+
+Pull requests run essential source, dependency and captured-regression checks by default. Real Docker image builds and container integration in `docker-pr-check` require the optional `ENABLE_DOCKER_PR_BUILDS=true` repository variable; their scripts and assertions remain available. Default-branch Docker publication still builds the actual release images after npm publication. An opt-in PR build is additional coverage, not a replacement for default-branch production qualification.
+
+Pull request events and explicit dispatches on actual feature branches use the named `pr-essential` source-test profile through the existing shared runner. Selected tests retain their `default` membership; default-branch pushes and dispatches still run the full default unit suite automatically. No PR-number input or checkout override is introduced. GitHub integration tests and their credential resolution run only in that full branch lane with `ENABLE_REAL_GITHUB_E2E=true`. The profile covers captured client evidence, model and dependency contracts, mocked coding/draft/reporting, prompts, Docker source policy, source-file size constraints and suite selection; it does not claim full PR or real-client acceptance.

+{"body":"Fixes #337

## Summary

The only red run on `008ec1c`, JS CI/CD [39827151731](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/39827151731), was a false positive. It also hid a release that never shipped. I swept every run on that commit for more false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors (logs in [`dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-337-49d8f27200a3/dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338)), compared the pipeline with the [js](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template), [rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) and [python](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) pipeline templates and with hive-mind's [`CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md), and fixed each defect wherever it occurs.

FP = red without a real defect, FN = green while something is wrong, W = warning.

| # | Kind | Defect | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | FP | `run-with-budget-warning.sh` killed a command up to 1 s early: bash's `SECONDS` counts second *boundaries*, so `-ge budget` fired after `budget - 1 + ε` s. This failed the macOS unit tests and skipped the release of #334. | `-gt` deadlines. Also ports the JS template's hardened wrapper, with `BUDGET_VERBOSE` tracing (off by default). | `js/tests/run-with-budget-warning.js` (deterministic, starts just before a second boundary), `experiments/issue-337/budget-early-kill.mjs` |
| D2 | FN, W | Rust lint passed with clippy and rustdoc warnings | `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, `check-cargo-warnings.sh`. Warnings fixed. | the CI lint job itself |
| D3 | FP/FN | The changeset check counted every changeset on disk, including the unreleased one from #334 | Count only the files the PR adds (JS changesets and Rust fragments) | `js/tests/validate-changeset.js` |
| D5 | W | `EBADENGINE` for `@opentui/core` (needs Node ≥ 26.4) | Node 26 in every `setup-node` | install logs |
| D6 | W, FN | `allowScripts` named `node-pty@1.2.0-beta.15` while the lockfile has `1.1.0`, so the install script was skipped | Pin refreshed; `strict-allow-scripts` turns future drift into an error | install logs |

| D8 | FP annotation | `##[error] No Trusted Publishing config` on a green Rust release | The OIDC step runs only when `vars.CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING == 'true'`; a notice explains the token fallback | — |
| D9 | W | lychee `No files found` for `./**/*.html` | Directory input with `--extensions md,html` | links run log |
| D10 | FN | Instant Release could publish without lint or tests | `needs` + `success` checks on lint, test, verbose-integration and package-install | `js/tests/workflow-policy.js` "release gating" |
| D11 | FN | A first-attempt instant release ended green without publishing when main moved | Only a rerun (`GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT > 1`) counts as finishing an earlier attempt (`scripts/release-rerun.mjs`) | `js/tests/ci-scripts.js` |

A cancellation passes only if a newer commit replaced the run (`git ls-remote refs/pull/<n>/head`) **and** the job's `cancel-in-progress` evaluates to true (`scripts/job-cancel-policy.mjs`). Gates added to every workflow. `PIPELINE_STATUS_VERBOSE=1` traces each decision. | `js/tests/check-pipeline-status.js` (16 cases), `js/tests/workflow-policy.js` |

## How to reproduce D1

```bash
git show d274daa^:scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh > /tmp/old-budget.sh
node experiments/issue-337/budget-early-kill.mjs /tmp/old-budget.sh
# BUG: a command shorter than its budget was terminated (1.4 s command, 2 s budget, killed after 1.40 s)
node experiments/issue-337/budget-early-kill.mjs
# OK: the command finished inside its budget and was not terminated
cd js && bun test tests/run-with-budget-warning.js
```

Each report includes a reproduction (the gate reports use `experiments/issue-337/template-gate-*.sh`, which take a template clone as their argument), a workaround and a suggested fix.

## Needs a maintainer

- **crates.io trusted publishing:** a crates.io owner of `link-assistant-agent` must add this repository and `rust.yml` as a trusted publisher, then set the repository variable `CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING=true`. See [`open-findings.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/blob/issue-337-49d8f27200a3/dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338/open-findings.md):

+{"body":"Fixes #335

## Summary

This ports the reliability fixes that upstream [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) made after our fork point (`0068cb305f`, 2025-11-19, up to `d93568f334`) to the tools, session loop, provider layer and MCP client we already have. **No tools were added.** Each fix applies to code we already have, and each has a regression test.

Upstream moved its code twice since the fork (to Effect services, then from `packages/opencode` to `packages/core`), so no upstream commit could be cherry-picked. I listed all 900 upstream `fix` commits that touch tools, session, provider or MCP code (`docs/case-studies/issue-335/data/`), triaged each one as PORT, ALREADY-HAVE or N/A (`analysis/A–D`), and re-implemented the PORT items in JS. Where a defect also exists in the Rust port, it is fixed in Rust too.

Full case study, including the requirements, timeline, method, online research, libraries considered and verification: [`docs/case-studies/issue-335/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-335-cc63abda9307/docs/case-studies/issue-335).

## What changed

### Edit and write (JS + Rust)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |

## Review follow-up: compatibility, memory, Rust parity

Answer to the review comment ("not break anything previously working … configuration for breaking changes … memory leaks … parity between JavaScript and Rust"). Details: §11 of the case study and the audits in `experiments/issue-335/audit/`.

**Backward compatibility.** The JSON input format, event types and envelope are unchanged; stored sessions still load. Every change a script or model could notice has a switch that restores the previous behaviour, as a CLI flag and a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env var (JS `src/config/config.ts`, Rust `src/compat.rs`):

| Change | Restore previous behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| bash runs `$SHELL` (if POSIX) or bash instead of `/bin/sh` | `--bash-shell legacy` (or a path) |
| bash keeps the tail of long output; edit/write return a confirmation; read past EOF is an error | `--legacy-tool-output` |
| edit refuses loose fuzzy matches and an empty `oldString` on an existing file | `--legacy-edit-matching` |
| glob/ls do not follow symlinked directories | `--glob-follow-symlinks` |
| grep searches hidden files and stops after 30 s | `--no-grep-hidden`, `--grep-timeout-ms 0` |
| read returns at most 2000 lines / 50 KB | `--read-max-lines 0`, `--read-max-bytes 0` |
| context overflow is reported as `ContextOverflowError` | `--legacy-error-names` (non-retryable `APIError`, as before) |
| `tokens.output` excludes reasoning tokens | `--legacy-token-usage` |
| a `stop` finish after tool calls continues the loop | `--legacy-loop-exit` |
| MCP connect is bounded (30 s) | `--mcp-connect-timeout 0` or per-server `connect_timeout` |

MCP `timeout` keeps its old meaning (tools listing); connect got its own `connect_timeout` so that a short listing timeout no longer cuts a slow connect. `js/tests/compat-flags.ts` runs every switch in both states and checks the env wiring in a child process; the Rust switches are tested through `ToolContext::with_settings`.

**Memory and resource leaks fixed (JS):** unbounded SSE usage map; the usage tee branch that stopped reading and made the tee buffer the rest of the stream; bash output and abort-listener retention; grep buffering all rg output; FileTime stamps after a session is deleted; continuous/single-shot mode waiting forever for `session.idle` when a prompt failed early; retried 5xx/429 bodies not cancelled; retry `sleep` abort listener; `withTimeout` timer on rejection; `Instance.dispose()` leaving the cache entry; pending permission asks of a cancelled turn. Each has a regression test. Two items were left on purpose (client disconnect does not cancel a turn; the per-request provider timeout signal) — reasons in §11.2.

**Rust parity.** `grep`, `glob`, `list`, `read`, `edit`, `bash`, `todo`, `batch`, `webfetch`, `websearch` now match the JS tools (output, errors, limits; edit diffs checked against output of the JS code), with the same compatibility switches plus `--read-only` / `--disable-tools`. Latent Rust bugs fixed: non-ASCII panic in `permission.rs`, prefix match in `Filesystem::contains`, panic on an empty id. Not done, with reasons: FileTime and the per-file lock (each Rust CLI run is a separate process with no session), permission checks in tools (the Rust CLI never runs tools for a model), and the absent LLM/session/provider/MCP layers (pre-existing). Divergences are listed in `experiments/issue-335/audit/rust-parity-fixes.md`.

**CI checks that also failed on `main`** (fixed here, no manual step; §11.4 of the case study):

- **Security:** `body-parser` 2.3.0 (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828, high), bumped to 2.4.0 in both lockfiles.
- **Free Model Drift:** Kilo withdrew `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`, the default model and first compaction model in JS and Rust. The defaults are now `kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (cascade `(kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free kilo/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free same)`). For backward compatibility `kilo/nemotron-3-super-free` (and the bare short name) stays accepted as a deprecated alias that runs on Ultra and logs a warning naming the replacement; the drift script skips aliases and checks that their targets are built-ins.
- **Model Catalogue:** `check-default-models.mjs` reported the same withdrawn default; fixed by the new default. The alias warning lives in `kilo-deprecation.ts` so `kilo.ts` stays dependency-free (this workflow runs without installing packages).
- **Dependency Freshness:** all direct npm dependencies bumped to latest (AI SDK and `@ai-sdk/*`, MCP SDK, opentui 0.8, `glob` 14, `minimatch` 11, `hono`, `command-stream` 2.6, …; no source changes needed). `solid-js` unpinned (opentui#689 is closed) and the obsolete `seroval` override dropped. `lino-arguments` stays on 0.3.x and is pinned: 0.4.0 makes the agent exit at startup when the host has both `http_proxy` and `HTTP_PROXY` (reported upstream: link-foundation/lino-arguments#50). Rust: `globset`, `ignore`, `similar` and `uuid` updated to their latest patch releases for `cargo outdated`.

**Crash in git worktrees and submodules (found while checking the dependency refresh).** `Project.fromDirectory` wrote its id cache to `.git/opencode` without awaiting or handling the write. In a worktree or submodule `.git` is a file, so the write rejected with `ENOTDIR` and the `unhandledRejection` handler exited the CLI with code 1, on every run. The id is now cached in the common git dir (as upstream does) and a failed write is only logged. Reproduction: `bun experiments/issue-335/project-worktree.ts <worktree dir>`; regression test `js/tests/project-worktree.ts` fails before the fix and passes after.

## Deliberate deviations from upstream

- **No new tools** (requirement of the issue): `apply_patch`, `lsp`, `question`, `skill`, `plan-*` and `code-mode` were not added. The unregistered `patch` and `multiedit` stay unregistered.
- **`write` keeps "no restrictions"**: upstream requires a prior read; the fork removed that on purpose (`db682c8`).
- **Image formats**: upstream stopped sending SVG/BMP/TIFF/ICO/AVIF as images (#21114). The fork supports them on a maintainer's request (`86f24ac`), so that change was not ported.
- After an overflow compaction, upstream replays the user message; here the existing flow (summary plus a synthetic "Continue if you have next steps") is kept.

Known remaining limitation: when a model overflows, the compaction model cascade does not move on to the next model; the overflow is reported instead.

## How to reproduce (example: lost parallel edits)

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/main origin/main && cp -r experiments/issue-335 /tmp/main/experiments/
ln -s "$PWD/js/node_modules" /tmp/main/js/node_modules
(cd /tmp/main && bun experiments/issue-335/edit-write/01-parallel-edits.ts)
# runs=20 both-fulfilled-but-one-edit-lost=15 rejected=1
bun experiments/issue-335/edit-write/01-parallel-edits.ts
# runs=20 both-fulfilled-but-one-edit-lost=0 rejected=0
```

Other reproductions are in `experiments/issue-335/{edit-write,read-search,bash-web}/`.

## Summary

The only red run on `008ec1c`, JS CI/CD [39827151731](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/39827151731), was a false positive. It also hid a release that never shipped. I swept every run on that commit for more false positives, false negatives, warnings and errors (logs in [`dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-337-49d8f27200a3/dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338)), compared the pipeline with the [js](https://github.com/link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template), [rust](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) and [python](https://github.com/link-foundation/python-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template) pipeline templates and with hive-mind's [`CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/main/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md), and fixed each defect wherever it occurs.

FP = red without a real defect, FN = green while something is wrong, W = warning.

| # | Kind | Defect | Fix | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| D1 | FP | `run-with-budget-warning.sh` killed a command up to 1 s early: bash's `SECONDS` counts second *boundaries*, so `-ge budget` fired after `budget - 1 + ε` s. This failed the macOS unit tests and skipped the release of #334. | `-gt` deadlines. Also ports the JS template's hardened wrapper, with `BUDGET_VERBOSE` tracing (off by default). | `js/tests/run-with-budget-warning.js` (deterministic, starts just before a second boundary), `experiments/issue-337/budget-early-kill.mjs` |
| D2 | FN, W | Rust lint passed with clippy and rustdoc warnings | `RUSTFLAGS=-Dwarnings`, `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings`, `check-cargo-warnings.sh`. Warnings fixed. | the CI lint job itself |
| D3 | FP/FN | The changeset check counted every changeset on disk, including the unreleased one from #334 | Count only the files the PR adds (JS changesets and Rust fragments) | `js/tests/validate-changeset.js` |
| D5 | W | `EBADENGINE` for `@opentui/core` (needs Node ≥ 26.4) | Node 26 in every `setup-node` | install logs |

| D9 | W | lychee `No files found` for `./**/*.html` | Directory input with `--extensions md,html` | links run log |
| D10 | FN | Instant Release could publish without lint or tests | `needs` + `success` checks on lint, test, verbose-integration and package-install | `js/tests/workflow-policy.js` "release gating" |

A cancellation passes only if a newer commit replaced the run (`git ls-remote refs/pull/<n>/head`) **and** the job's `cancel-in-progress` evaluates to true (`scripts/job-cancel-policy.mjs`). Gates added to every workflow. `PIPELINE_STATUS_VERBOSE=1` traces each decision. | `js/tests/check-pipeline-status.js` (16 cases), `js/tests/workflow-policy.js` |

Full analysis, each defect with its evidence, the timeline, every requirement with its status, the options considered, and the components surveyed: [`dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-337-49d8f27200a3/dev/log/issues/337/pulls/338).

## How to reproduce D1


Each report includes a reproduction (the gate reports use `experiments/issue-337/template-gate-*.sh`, which take a template clone as their argument), a workaround and a suggested fix.

- **crates.io trusted publishing:** a crates.io owner of `link-assistant-agent` must add this repository and `rust.yml` as a trusted publisher, then set the repository variable `CRATES_IO_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING=true`. ## Problem

In [the failing release run](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/36386196804), Changesets reported `@link-assistant/agent@0.26.6` published at 06:25:40Z. The seven registry checks ended at 06:27:41Z, 120 seconds later; npm exposed the version six seconds afterward. The job failed before creating the GitHub release.

## Changes

- Poll npm's exact `versions` entry with exponential backoff for five minutes (13 checks), succeeding as soon as the version appears. Record when the publish command succeeded even if verification later times out.
- On a release rerun, sync the checkout to current `main`. If its package version is already on npm, complete a missing tag, GitHub release, or release-note formatting without republishing. A late tag points to the version bump commit.
- Add an always-running release summary that distinguishes npm publication with incomplete post-steps from a version that was not published. Cover both automatic and manual release jobs.
- Create the missing [js-v0.26.6 GitHub release](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/releases/tag/js-v0.26.6) with the pipeline's formatted changelog notes. Its tag points to the 0.26.6 version commit.
- Match the exact npm badge footer before treating release notes as formatted; a misleading URL cannot skip formatting.
- Preserve the confirmed npm publication state if the GitHub release lookup fails, so the summary reports incomplete post-steps correctly.
- Normalize workflow line endings in the wiring test so Windows checkout uses the same assertions.
- Extend the pending patch changeset on `main` so the repository keeps its one changeset per PR rule.

## Reproduction and verification

- Before the fix, the polling test failed: `Received: 120000`, `Expected: >= 300000` milliseconds. The fake registry returns 404 for 20 seconds and then exposes the exact version; the helper succeeds on the fourth check.
- A mocked dry run starts with the version already on npm and no GitHub release, then records tag/release creation and changelog formatting in order, with no publish call. Tests also cover an existing release whose notes still need formatting and a misleading badge URL. The latter test failed before the fix. Workflow wiring checks run against both LF and CRLF text, reproducing the Windows CI failure before normalization.
- A new regression confirms npm publication remains recorded when GitHub release lookup fails; it failed before the fix and passes afterward. The workflow wiring test passes with both LF and CRLF input, addressing the Windows CI failure in [run 36610180845](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/36610180845).
- After merging current `main` locally: `bun run test` passed (808 passed, 4 existing todos, 0 failed); the focused release tests (43 passed), `npm run check`, changeset validation, Docker actionlint, and `npm audit --audit-level=high --package-lock-only` passed. The audit found 0 high and 0 critical vulnerabilities.

## Summary

This ports the reliability fixes that upstream [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) made after our fork point (`0068cb305f`, 2025-11-19, up to `d93568f334`) to the tools, session loop, provider layer and MCP client we already have. **No tools were added.** Each fix applies to code we already have, and each has a regression test.

Upstream moved its code twice since the fork (to Effect services, then from `packages/opencode` to `packages/core`), so no upstream commit could be cherry-picked. I listed all 900 upstream `fix` commits that touch tools, session, provider or MCP code (`docs/case-studies/issue-335/data/`), triaged each one as PORT, ALREADY-HAVE or N/A (`analysis/A–D`), and re-implemented the PORT items in JS. Where a defect also exists in the Rust port, it is fixed in Rust too.

Full case study, including the requirements, timeline, method, online research, libraries considered and verification: [`docs/case-studies/issue-335/`](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/tree/issue-335-cc63abda9307/docs/case-studies/issue-335).

## What changed

### Edit and write (JS + Rust)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Parallel edits of one file lost updates | #4388, #23483 | Per-file lock (`FileTime.withLock`) for `edit` and `write` |
| Loose fuzzy match could replace unrelated code; empty `oldString` overwrote a file | #30932 | Stricter thresholds, size guard, explicit error |
| CRLF / mixed endings / UTF-8 BOM not preserved | #9443, #53166, #23797 | Endings and BOM kept; untouched lines never rewritten |
| `replaceAll` interpreted `$&`, `$1` | — | Literal replacement |
| False "modified since read" (clock comparison, `dir/./a` vs `dir/a`) | #17835, #20367 | `{mtime, size}` stamp, canonical path keys |
| `edit` right after `write` failed; empty tool output | `66f9bdab32` | `write` records a read; short confirmations |

### Read, grep, glob, ls (JS + Rust)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `glob`/`ls` hung after 100 results (rg blocked on a full pipe) | #10833 | Stream cancelled and rg killed; abort passed through |
| `grep` dropped all matches when one path was unreadable (rg exit 2) | #8612 | Matches kept, plus a note |
| `grep` deadlock on large stderr, no cancel, hidden files skipped | #39238, #7501 | Pipes drained together, abort + 30 s timeout, `--hidden` without `.git` |
| `read` relative to the worktree root, unbounded output, whole file read for the binary check, `\r` leaked | `6cf2c3e3db`, #14009, #51011 | Session directory, 50 KB cap, 4 KB sample, CRLF split |
| macOS screenshot names (U+202F, curly quotes) "not found" | #45807, #50953 | Unique entry matched after canonicalizing |

### Bash and web tools (JS + Rust)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bash` ran `/bin/sh` (dash), so bash syntax failed | #3494, #5205 | `$SHELL` if usable, otherwise bash (zsh on macOS) |
| Long output kept the start and dropped the end, where errors are; UTF-8 split (Rust panic) | #22660, #39403 | Tail kept on character boundaries |
| `echo x > file` passed an `echo*` allow rule in read-only/plan mode | #6737 | Write redirects checked as a separate `>` command |
| Rust `bash` deadlocked on full stderr and lost output on timeout | (found here) | Concurrent pipes, partial output, signal reported |
| Web tools: timeout did not cover the body; 5 MB limit checked only after reading it all; Cloudflare 403; Exa key ignored | #21378, #33259, #10328, #16362 | `AbortSignal.timeout`, bounded streaming reader, one honest retry, shared Exa client |
| `Tool.define` stacked wrappers on each init; `task` leaked its subscription | #16952, #9992 | Copy before wrap; `try/finally` |

### Session loop, provider transforms, MCP (JS only; Rust has none of these yet)

| Defect | Upstream | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Context overflow (400 "prompt is too long", 413, `context_length_exceeded`) ended the session | #6480, #14707 | `ContextOverflowError` → compact and continue; a second overflow stops with a clear error |
| Finish `stop` after tool calls ended the loop before the results were sent back | #14973, #26178 | Loop continues while the last step has completed tool calls |
| Retryable 5xx stream errors, plain-text rate limits, Vertex exhaustion, OpenAI item 404, `ZlibError` not retried | #12768, #10590, #24063, #19104 | Classified as retryable; delays capped at 2³¹−1 ms |
| `retry-after` beyond the retry timeout: `process()` returned `undefined` and the loop started another step | (found here) | Normal final-error path, turn stops; retry-only errors added to the message error union (saving them threw a `ZodError`) |
| Lone surrogates, empty Anthropic/Bedrock blocks, empty user messages, foreign signatures/reasoning → 400 | #25934, #4811, `021e42c0bb1`, #21370 | Sanitized per target model |
| Shallow-spread cache options, wrong Bedrock cache point, Moonshot schema errors | #10323, #11664, #18959, #24730, #11984 | `mergeDeep`, `cachePoint: { type: 'default' }`, schema fixes |
| Interrupted tools lost their start time; raw string tool input broke Gemini; tool events without `tool-input-start` dropped | #27254, #21709 | `interrupted` marker, `{ value }` wrapping, `ensureToolCall` |
| Reasoning tokens charged twice; Anthropic thinking budget branch never ran | #21047, (found here) | Charged once; `model.npm` passed |
| MCP: no connect or `tools/list` timeout, endless pagination, sequential listing, leaked failed clients, silent removal on bad URL, no-tools servers failed, results without `content` dropped, timed-out calls kept running, `_` in server names broke per-tool timeouts, connect timeout was `NaN`, grandchildren left on dispose | #6760, #19200, #31442, #13229, #25019, #31595, #31271, #7879, #32244, #15516 | All fixed; see §6.3 of the case study |

## Review follow-up: compatibility, memory, Rust parity

**Backward compatibility.** The JSON input format, event types and envelope are unchanged; stored sessions still load. Every change a script or model could notice has a switch that restores the previous behaviour, as a CLI flag and a `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_*` env var (JS `src/config/config.ts`, Rust `src/compat.rs`):

| Change | Restore previous behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| bash runs `$SHELL` (if POSIX) or bash instead of `/bin/sh` | `--bash-shell legacy` (or a path) |
| bash keeps the tail of long output; edit/write return a confirmation; read past EOF is an error | `--legacy-tool-output` |

Not done, with reasons: FileTime and the per-file lock (each Rust CLI run is a separate process with no session), permission checks in tools (the Rust CLI never runs tools for a model), and the absent LLM/session/provider/MCP layers (pre-existing). Divergences are listed in `experiments/issue-335/audit/rust-parity-fixes.md`.

- **Security:** `body-parser` 2.3.0 (GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828, high), bumped to 2.4.0 in both lockfiles.
- **Free Model Drift:** Kilo withdrew `nvidia/nemotron-3-super-120b-a12b:free`, the default model and first compaction model in JS and Rust. The defaults are now `kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (cascade `(kilo/nemotron-3-ultra-free kilo/nemotron-3.5-lightning-free same)`). For backward compatibility `kilo/nemotron-3-super-free` (and the bare short name) stays accepted as a deprecated alias that runs on Ultra and logs a warning naming the replacement; the drift script skips aliases and checks that their targets are built-ins.

## Problem

JS CI/CD run [33551125228](https://github.com/link-assistant/agent/actions/runs/33551125228)
went red on `main` with

```
Error updating npm: $ is not a function
```

after all six checks had passed. Auditing that run end to end surfaced a second
class of problem: several steps could not have failed the pipeline even when
they were broken, and the release gates could not tell a timeout from a pass.

## Root cause of the reported failure

`use-m` resolves a package with `createRequire(...).resolve`, so the `require`
condition wins and `command-stream@>=0.19.0` is loaded through its **CommonJS**
entry point. Node.js 23+ adds a synthetic `'module.exports'` named export to
CommonJS namespaces, which `use-m` does not recognise as metadata, so it stops
unwrapping the callable default:

```console
$ npx --yes node@24 --input-type=module -e "…const loaded = await use('command-stream')…"
{"node":"v24.20.0","keys":["default","module.exports"],"dollar":"undefined","defaultDollar":"function"}

$ npx --yes node@20 …
{"node":"v20.20.2","keys":["AnsiUtils",…,"$","default"],"dollar":"function","defaultDollar":"function"}
```

`const { $ } = await use('command-stream')` therefore yields `undefined`, and the
first tagged template throws. `scripts/use-module.mjs` normalizes the namespace on
every Node version; the eight release scripts now go through it.

## What changed

**False negatives — CI could not fail**

- A job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported by GitHub as *cancelled*, not
  failed, and every release gate reads `needs.<job>.result == 'success'`, so a

Fixes #334. The agent now supports every AI provider that [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) supports, the OpenAI-compatible services and local API of [gpt4free](https://github.com/xtekky/gpt4free), and live model discovery, so new models work without an agent release or a docs edit.

### Providers (OpenCode parity)

OpenCode's providers are the [models.dev](https://models.dev) catalogue plus provider-specific code in its loaders and auth plugins. Both parts are covered here.

- **Every models.dev provider loads** (`js/src/provider/env-template.ts`, `provider.ts`). Base URLs with `${ENV}` templates (Cloudflare, Databricks, Snowflake Cortex, Vertex, Neon and others) are filled from the environment the same way OpenCode fills them. Per-model endpoints are honoured. Variables that only name an account, region or project are never sent as an API key.
- **Custom loaders ported from OpenCode** (`js/src/provider/parity-loaders.ts`):
  - Amazon Bedrock, including Mantle, with cross-region prefixes;
  - Google Vertex: ADC through `google-auth-library` and the regional `aiplatform.googleapis.com` hosts;
  - Cloudflare AI Gateway and Workers AI;
  - Snowflake Cortex and SAP AI Core;
  - Venice and AIHubMix, which fall back to their OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
- **Subscription logins ported to `agent auth login`** (`js/src/auth/provider-logins.ts`, `azure-login.ts`):
  - xAI (SuperGrok) device login, with token refresh;
  - Poe browser login (PKCE) and DigitalOcean browser login;
  - GitLab (gitlab.com and self-managed);
  - Azure Microsoft Entra ID through the Azure CLI. It uses a bearer token per audience, `cognitiveservices` or the Foundry `ai.azure.com`.

  These join the existing Claude, ChatGPT, Copilot, Google, Qwen and Kilo logins.
- **`prompt_cache_key`** is sent to the openai-compatible providers OpenCode enables it for (`transform.ts`).

**Not ported, on purpose:**
- **OpenCode's _Console_ login.** It signs in to OpenCode's own organisation control plane with OpenCode's client identity, so another client cannot use it. OpenCode Zen models still work with `OPENCODE_API_KEY`.
- **Listing Azure deployments through the Azure management API.** The agent uses the data-plane deployments listing instead, which accepts both API keys and Entra ID tokens.

Both are documented in `docs/providers.md` and `docs/model-discovery.md`.

### gpt4free

Added in `js/src/provider/extra-providers.ts` and documented in `docs/gpt4free.md`:

- **`gpt4free`** (`g4f`): the local Interference API. `G4F_PROVIDER` routes requests to one of gpt4free's providers via `/api/{provider}`.
- **`g4f-space`**: the hosted gateway.
- **`pollinations`**.
- **Key-based OpenAI-compatible services from gpt4free's provider list**: `airforce`, `aibadgr`, `api-route`, `cheaperinference` and `theb`.
- **Local servers**: `ollama`, `vllm`, `llamacpp` and `omniroute`. `lmstudio` (from models.dev) is made keyless.

The rest of gpt4free's providers fall into two groups. Most are services models.dev already lists, such as OpenRouter, Groq, DeepInfra, Together, Cerebras and Nvidia. The others scrape web apps or need a browser session, so they are only reachable through the gpt4free API.

Keyless providers are **explicit-only**: they never become the default and never answer a short model name, so a stray local server cannot take over a run. Routers and local servers pass unknown model IDs through unchanged.

### Dynamic model info (ideas from hive-mind)

Added `js/src/provider/model-discovery.ts` and the `agent models --discover / --refresh / --free` options:

- **Live listings.** Each provider's own token-free listing endpoint (`/models`, Anthropic, Google, Cohere, Azure deployments, Vercel AI Gateway, Kilo) adds models released since the last models.dev update. models.dev only supplies their metadata.
- **Hive-mind rules.** Endpoints that spend tokens are refused before any request. Results are cached for at least one hour. The cache key covers the provider, the URL and a scrypt fingerprint of the credential.
- **Unknown `--model`.** The agent refreshes models.dev, then checks the live listing, then passes the ID through for routers. Otherwise it fails clearly instead of switching to another model.
- **Opt-out.** `LINK_ASSISTANT_AGENT_MODEL_DISCOVERY=off` disables live listings.

### Docs

- **New:** `docs/providers.md`, `docs/gpt4free.md` and `docs/model-discovery.md`.
  - `docs/providers.md` covers credentials, logins and parity notes. It also has a generated table of all models.dev providers: run `bun scripts/generate-provider-docs.mjs`, or add `--check` to verify it.
- **Refreshed:** `MODELS.md` and `FREE_MODELS.md` now list current models, and the usage examples put free models (Kilo, gpt4free, Pollinations, local servers) before paid ones.
- **Updated:** `README.md` and `js/README.md` link to the new pages.

Fixes #332. A tool call that fails and is recovered from (`read` on a missing file, a bad edit anchor, a non-zero `bash` exit) is no longer emitted as a top-level `{"type":"error"}` event. That type is reserved for failures that end the turn or the session, which is how Hive Mind treats it.

### Root cause

`js/src/cli/event-handler.js` (`outputBusEvent`) emitted **two** events for every failed tool part: the `tool_use` event, which already carries `part.state.status: "error"` and the error text, and a duplicate top-level `type: "error"` event (written to stderr). In the incident log, Hive Mind saw that duplicate and logged *"Agent exited 0 after an error event; the error event in its output still fails the run"*, and the run failed with `Agent reported error: Error: File not found: …/e.g`. The model had in fact read the tool result, finished the turn with `reason: "stop"`, and the agent had exited 0.

The Claude `stream-json` adapter depended on the duplicate: it turned the `error` event back into the terminal `tool_result` with `status: "error"`. Because the source event was an `error`, that `tool_result` went to **stderr** instead of stdout.

### Changes

- `js/src/cli/event-handler.js`: a failed tool call is reported only on its `tool_use` event. Top-level `error` events now come only from `session.error` and the CLI-level failure paths.
- `js/src/json-standard/index.ts`: the Claude adapter builds the error `tool_result` directly from the `tool_use` snapshot (`errorText(state.error, 'Tool execution failed')`). It now goes to stdout like every other tool result. The tool-specific branch of the `error` case was removed.
- `docs/stdin-mode.md` → *Error Events*: documents the contract. `error` means the turn or session failed, and a failed tool call shows up only as `tool_use` with `state.status: "error"` (OpenCode) or `tool_result` with `status: "error"` (Claude). `js/README.md` links to it.
- Case study: `docs/case-studies/issue-332/README.md`. Changeset: patch.

Of the options listed in the issue, I chose "report only on `tool_use`" over a new `tool_error` type or a `recoverable: true` flag. The information is already on the `tool_use` event, and a separate event would be one more type for consumers to classify.

### How to reproduce / tests

- **`js/tests/recoverable-tool-error.ts`** (new, end to end): runs the real CLI against a local OpenAI-compatible mock. The first turn calls `read` on a missing file and the follow-up turn answers with text. For both `--json-standard opencode` and `claude` the test asserts that:
  - the model received `File not found`,
  - the failure appears on the tool's own event (Claude: on stdout, not stderr),
  - the model continued and the exit code is 0,
  - **the stream contains no `error` event**.

  Before the fix, both tests failed and showed exactly the event from the incident (`{"type":"error",…,"message":"Error: File not found: …/e.g"}`).
- **`js/tests/event-handler.js`**: the two #289 tests that asserted the old duplicate event were replaced. A failed tool part, with or without error detail, now yields only `tool_use` and does not call `onError`. A `session.error` is still a fatal `error` with a readable `message`. The Claude error `tool_result` goes to stdout, renders object errors, and falls back to `Tool execution failed`.

Locally, before the fix: 5 of the new or changed tests fail. After the fix: `npm test` reports 874 pass, 0 fail, and `npm run check` (eslint, prettier, file size) is clean.

### Note for consumers

OpenCode-format consumers that used the duplicate `error` event to detect tool failures should read `part.state.status === "error"` on `tool_use` instead. Hive Mind's side is tracked in link-assistant/hive-mind#3213.

### Housekeeping

- Removed `js/.changeset/served-free-models.md`. Its content was already released in full in 0.26.13 (and partly in 0.26.12), but the file stayed on `main`, so it failed the one-changeset-per-PR check and would have been released a third time. This follows the same precedent as `d5ea9bd`.
- Removed the auto-generated `.gitkeep` placeholder.
